reason: The text demonstrates Yahweh's protective commitment to the Hebrew people (Judah) through multiple expressions: (1) God hears Hezekiah's prayer (וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֨ל חִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָה), (2) Isaiah delivers God's promise of deliverance responding to the Assyrian threat, (3) God explicitly commits to defending Jerusalem (וְגַנּוֹתִ֛י אֶל־ הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את לְהֽוֹשִׁיעָ֑הּ), and (4) God miraculously destroys the entire Assyrian army (185,000 soldiers) in a single night, completely resolving the existential threat to the people. The narrative arc shows divine intervention specifically to preserve the Hebrew nation from destruction, which constitutes a clear expression of God's desire for their well-being.
